blindSummary:
This state/province was one of five regional authorities that formally adopted an "anti-LGBT ideology" resolution by mid-2020, helping place approximately one-third of the country's territory under declarations whose stated purpose was to exclude LGBTQ public events. It sits in the contiguous belt of conservative regional resolutions around a major metropolitan area. The resolution was struck down or repealed in the 2021 wave following the supranational body's funding threats.

No march ban, coordinated attack, or county-level holdout comparable to the late holdouts documented elsewhere in the country is recorded for this state/province; the finding is the resolution itself and its location in the country's conservative-region belt, and the practical visitor-facing exposure is that belt's general social climate rather than a specific enforcement or violence event.
blindSourceSummaries: Encyclopedia overview of the country's 'LGBT-free zones': by June 2020 some 100 municipalities and five regional authorities - this state/province among them - had adopted resolutions covering about a third of the country; mostly lobbied for by a conservative legal institute, legally meaningless but stigmatising; by 6 February 2024 the national capital's administrative court had repealed the last such declaration, and by 24 April 2025 all had been withdrawn or invalidated.

Legal-overview article on the rise and fall of the country's LGBT-free zones: between 2019 and 2025 more than 100 local governments adopted 'LGBT ideology'-free resolutions or family-rights charters drafted by a conservative legal institute, covering about a third of the country at the movement's peak; the documents created no criminal penalties but symbolically sidelined LGBT residents from civic life; litigation by the national human-rights commissioner led courts to strike them down as unconstitutional, a supranational funding body threatened to freeze billions in regional funds, and the last remaining zone was abolished in spring 2025.
blindTangential: The state/province resolution was an anti-LGBT-ideology declaration (LGBT broadly, not trans-specific) and is formally gone; the visitor-facing residue is a general civic climate in the conservative-region belt rather than any enforcement or violence event documented for this unit.
